_comment: Single source of truth for workflow SHAPE (the second axis). The task-type registry says what each node SAYS (routing + workflow prose); THIS registry says the node SEQUENCE — which agents a workflow runs, in what order, its verify policy, its stop condition, AND which checkpoint verifiers it fans out. The shape is PARTIALLY LOAD-BEARING: the `verifiers` field drives the checkpoint fan-out (dispatch.py cmd_dispatch_next + _step_emit_dispatch_batch iterate verifiers_for(shape)), so a project shape omitting test-runner simply doesn't fan it out. The `nodes` topology STAYS ADVISORY: shape_allows (dispatch.py) consults it only to attach a `shape_violation` disclosure when an action's agent is off-topology — never to block or reroute — and the planner→executor→checker spine runs unchanged regardless of the resolved shape. (nodes is the SPINE topology; verifiers are its checkpoint CHILDREN — distinct lists, never conflated: a phase-checker dispatching a verifier is on-topology even though the verifier is not in nodes.) The other accessors (verify_policy_for / stop_condition_for / instruction_for) feed `registry-doc --shape` display ONLY — `instruction_for` is NOT injected into an orchestrator prompt (contrast the task-type `workflow` field, which IS). So setting `research-first` surfaces `shape_violation` disclosures but does NOT run explorer first. (A project may still overlay conductor/workflow/workflow-shapes.json — opt-in by file presence — to add or override shapes with zero plugin edits; the rows resolve, render, and — for the verifier axis — drive the fan-out.)

_fields.nodes: the ordered list of SPINE dispatch agents this shape runs (the topology). Action tokens: spec-planner | explorer | task-executor | phase-checker. ADVISORY: shape_allows consults this only to surface a `shape_violation` disclosure when an off-topology agent dispatches — it does NOT block. Checkpoint verifiers (ac-tracer / test-runner) are NOT spine nodes; they are checkpoint children declared in `verifiers` below, and a phase-checker dispatching one is on-topology regardless of `nodes`.
_fields.verifiers: the ordered verifier-agent list fanned out at this shape's checkpoint (checkpoint CHILDREN of the spine — distinct from `nodes`, the spine topology). Each entry must be a verifier name (`ac-tracer` or `test-runner`). The fan-out emits one wave member per entry (the per-member envelope built inline by `_build_verifier`). Absent/empty => the standard [ac-tracer, test-runner] pair (fail-open). Unknown entries are dropped at fan-out. This is the load-bearing seam that makes a shape control WHICH verifiers its checkpoint runs.
_fields.requires: optional prerequisites the shape demands of track-state before it can run (advisory; future hook). Absent => no prerequisites.
_fields.verify_policy: how this shape gates progress: checkpoint (the default — phase-checker stamps a checkpoint gate) | none (no checkpoint gate — research/exploration shapes that produce no committable artifact).
_fields.stop_condition: what makes the shape DONE: all_nodes_done (every node in `nodes` has run) | a structured pass_condition. The fixed spine's default is all_nodes_done.
_fields.gates: the quality gates this shape enforces at the TRACK level — the ON/OFF each gate composes with the per-task exemption (a gate fires for a task iff (gate in gates) AND (not task_exempt)). Members: tdd (F2 red/green/refactor) | coverage (F3 >=80%) | checkpoint (F5 — the phase-checker checkpoint GATES progress; distinct from verify_policy, which is whether a checkpoint phase runs AT ALL). Absent/empty => the default shape's gates => the full set (today's behavior). The seam that lets a non-code shape drop F2/F3 at the track level while keeping the checkpoint.
_fields.ac_grounding: how acceptance criteria are GROUNDED for this shape. test (default) => ACs are grounded by test_TC_* functions (the basis of spec_integrity's grounding scan). review => ACs are grounded by an artifact anchor + a review attestation (a non-code deliverable shape — docs, design, research, a data deliverable), so the grounding scan reads anchors/attestations instead of test functions. A shape whose ACs ground another way declares it here so the grounding scan does not insist on test-grounding a non-test shape. Absent => test.
_fields.checkpoint_policy: whether this shape's checkpoint phase actually RUNS. run (default) => the phase-checker checkpoint fans out as normal (every shipped shape). skip-if-declared => short-circuit the checkpoint emit, but ONLY when the shape declares an integrity substitute (ac_grounding=review => the review attestation is the substitute); a skip-if-declared shape with NO declared substitute FAILS HARD (a shape_violation halt), never a silent skip. This is the 3rd load-bearing drives-dispatch field (after verifiers + gates); absent => run (today's behavior). The 'attach a guarantee to every freedom' invariant: checkpoint_policy must not become a second advisory nodes.
_fields.instruction: optional prompt-shaping prose for the orchestrator when this shape is active (mirrors the task-type `workflow` field). Absent => the orchestrator follows the default §3.0 dispatch loop.

default.instruction: The standard implement loop: spec-planner decomposes the brief into a plan, task-executor implements each task under the TDD/coverage gates, phase-checker verifies each phase and stamps the checkpoint. This is the shape the conductor has always run — declared here so it is data-driven, not hardcoded.

research-first.when_to_use: Declares the INTENDED topology for a research-heavy track — one whose first need is understanding (map the codebase / survey a dependency / spike an approach) before planning. ADVISORY: the conductor does NOT yet reorder dispatch by shape — today both shapes plan first, and this row documents intent + surfaces drift via `shape_violation` (e.g. when an `explorer` dispatch lands on a track whose shape omits it, or vice-versa). Pick this shape to RECORD that exploration should precede planning; making the conductor actually honor that ordering is a future code change at the dispatch emit site, not a registry edit.
research-first.instruction: ADVISORY — not injected today. Records the intent that, for a research-heavy track, explorer should run before spec-planner so the plan is decomposed with exploration findings in hand, and that no phase-checker checkpoint gates exploration (it produces no committable artifact). This prose is rendered by `registry-doc --shape research-first` for human/tooling reference; it is NOT injected into the orchestrator prompt, and the dispatch spine does not reorder to honor it. The shape surfaces a `shape_violation` disclosure if the agents actually dispatched drift off the declared `nodes`, so the misconfiguration is visible rather than silent.

migration.when_to_use: A behavior-PRESERVATION track — migrating code (framework upgrade, API rename, refactor across module boundaries) where correctness is witnessed by the EXISTING test suite, not new tests. The shape drops the tdd/coverage gates at the track level (gates=[checkpoint]): tasks owe a green existing suite at the checkpoint, not new tests or >=80% coverage. Pair with the [Migrate] task-type tag, whose `workflow` prose the executor fetches instead of TDD — the tag carries the executor guidance, the shape carries the gate paradigm (the conductor's two-registry separation: task-types own node behavior, shapes own topology + gates).
migration.instruction: The migration loop: spec-planner decomposes the migration into ordered, behavior-preserving tasks (each [Migrate]-tagged); task-executor implements each under the [Migrate] workflow (no new tests — keep the existing suite green); phase-checker fans out ac-tracer + test-runner at the checkpoint, where the existing suite is the behavior-preservation signal. This is the first non-code shape: the conductor's planner→executor→checker spine is unchanged — only the gates it enforces differ (tdd/coverage off, checkpoint on). Rendered by `registry-doc --shape migration`; the executor's per-task prose comes from `registry-doc --tag Migrate` (the tag, not this shape).

deliverable.when_to_use: A non-code DELIVERABLE track — producing an artifact that is NOT a tested code change (a design doc, a research report, a spec, a runbook, a data deliverable) where correctness is witnessed by an artifact anchor + a review attestation, not by automated tests. The shape drops the test-runner verifier (no tests to run — ac-tracer alone fans out at the checkpoint) and grounds ACs by review (ac_grounding=review), so each AC maps to a concrete deliverable anchor a reviewer attests rather than a test_TC_* function. Pair with a task-type tag whose `workflow` prose carries the executor guidance for producing the deliverable (the conductor's two-registry separation: task-types own node behavior, shapes own topology + grounding) — the tag carries the executor prose, the shape carries the verifier set + the grounding paradigm.
deliverable.instruction: The deliverable loop: spec-planner decomposes the deliverable into ordered tasks, each carrying an artifact anchor mapping its ACs to a concrete artifact (a doc section, a report chapter, a data file); task-executor produces each artifact under review-grounding (no tests — the AC is met by the anchor existing AND a review attesting it satisfies the criterion); phase-checker fans out ac-tracer ONLY (test-runner is dropped — there are no tests) at the checkpoint, where ac-tracer witnesses the declared AC anchors. The planner→executor→checker spine is unchanged from the default — only the verifier set (test-runner dropped) and the AC grounding (review not test) differ. Rendered by `registry-doc --shape deliverable`; the executor's per-task prose comes from the task-type tag (the tag, not this shape). A deliverable task still produces a real commit (a docs(conductor)/chore commit) so the F4 non-empty-commit_sha rule stays satisfied — the artifact is the commit's content.
